comments.value:
For one and three: get a group of friends together in a public and just vote kick anyone who shows up and cheats.

For the looking through walls, another thing you can do is have the camera out and turn off the environment layer. Possibly works better for looking around a big world for friends. I can think of a few ways that a world could prevent casual wall peeking, but using the camera would work around that.

Like if you peek into a wall and there is another wall. Or make some walls so thin you can see the person peeking and stab them?

Docteh: i myself tend to play alone on VRC or not with enough people to remove cheaters and some worlds completely turn off the whole VTK feature sadly so even if you had the people to call a VTK it wouldn't be effective on some worlds.

the camera could have a layer that cant be turned off that is designed for walls to prevent people from just doing that but it overlays with a greenscreen or whatever other effect needed so its seemless.

if a wall is thin and you can see them then yeah the whole concept that im showing is kinda not there BUT someone could watch you and if you get close they can just back away from it without that punishment of getting killed its why a screen should be blacked out alot like Half Life: Alyx, Blackout! does take a really good approach to this making it where you're unable to look through alot of the walls with a mirror or camera so that could also be a way to do it ig.

@{618ece8f22b63e309408b761|full_name}: I think for VRChat this is something that needs to be implemented in the world. I've seen world that hide other players beyond a certain distance.

For wall peeking in a game world the world can have a list of 3d areas that are part of the play area, if the camera isn't in a valid play area, can black out. 

But at the VRChat client level the software would have to do a path trace to determine if the object is visible or not.

@{62df7cd83e007e467295c4e1|full_name}: i mean developers can ofc implement it themselves yeah but if someone is starting out and has 0 idea on how to do that it would become difficult for them to do it when they're just wanting to make a game VRChat's physbones already exist so they could use a modified version of that that checks for the View since that is already a thing inside of the debug and make the walls have the physbones Touched property or Proximity property while having it as a world setting so this way a developer can just decide to allow it (by default it should roll out with it being turned on for every world so a developer can choose to turn it off themselves)

details:
Idea 1: Remove avatar colliders that let you fly or gain more speed, this should be added to prevent people from exploiting it on worlds like: Blackout, Prison Escape & more because it can make it where people on the Quest 2 & others cannot hit them entirely making the game unfair entirely.

(having it as a world setting would be good so people that want to explore a world can use a collider to fly and see the world & for game creators they can turn it off so people dont use it as a unfair advantage)

Idea 2: Disallow looking through walls, a system should be made where if you look through a wall your screen gets blacked out so you cant use that to cheat on games like: Murder 4, Prison Escape, Infested, Ghost & more so its a fair game all around. (having it as a world setting would be good so if someone makes a mini-game and doesnt want that to be happening they can turn it off and if a world creator doesnt mind it they can turn it on)

Idea 3: Distance-Based Tool Interaction Restrictions, if a tool isnt in proximity to the main player collider it shouldn't be able to be grabbed or messed with by a player for example: Murder 4 people can just use OVR to move their POV down towards weapons that they shouldn't have & people with 3rd party software can just abuse the grab function to effectively teleport all of the tools to them making a game unplayable.

i see things like this being abused in mini-games pretty often by people that wanna make the experience worse for people around them that're trying to play fair
title: Better World Creation Settings
